_note: Plain-language explanations of every field in a workspace config and in _default.json, shown by the Workspace Config Editor demo page. When you add a field to _default.json, explain it here too - in settings_fields, and each of its keys in settings_keys.

workspace_fields._note: Markdown shown on the workspace select page when this workspace is selected: summary, objectives, reading, videos. One string, or a list of blocks joined with blank lines. Images like screenshot.png load from the workspace's own folder.
workspace_fields._dev_note: Notes for developers. Never shown in the game - any field whose name starts with "_" is ignored.
workspace_fields.schema_version: The config format version. Always 1 for now.
workspace_fields.link_label: The labels key for this workspace's name, shown on its button in the workspace select page (e.g. "title_buttons_workspace_arp_ip"). Must exist in assets/labels/_default.json.
workspace_fields.include: 1 lists this workspace on the workspace select page, 0 hides it.
workspace_fields.category: Which workspace select section it's listed under: "admin", "attacker" or "defender".
workspace_fields.order: Its position within that section. Lower numbers come first; numbered sections show it as "1.", "2.", ...
workspace_fields.prerequisites: Workspaces to finish first, by page key (e.g. "workspaces/defender_ap_intro"). Not used by the game yet.
workspace_fields.estimated_minutes: Roughly how long the lesson takes. Not used by the game yet.
workspace_fields.gradable: Whether the lesson can be graded. Not used by the game yet.
workspace_fields.build_type: Must be "workspace" for a workspace page.
workspace_fields.settings: Only the settings this workspace changes from _default.json, where every option starts off (0). Turn on what the lesson needs: each form, model or column usually needs both its "available" entry and its *_shown entry set to 1. See the Settings Fields section below.
workspace_fields.title: The menu bar title, as the labels key "menu_bar_titles_<title>" (e.g. "arp_ip_workspace").
workspace_fields.menu_bar: The menu bar's buttons, left to right. Put the most important ones last: on a narrow window, buttons squash into the "..." menu from the left.
workspace_fields.layout_shape: The panel layout: exactly one group, {"h_panes_1": [...]} (side by side) or {"v_panes_1": [...]} (stacked), listing its contents in order. Each item is a panel id - its panel type plus a number, like "status_panel_1" - or another group of the same form. The same panel type can appear any number of times, as long as each copy has its own number ("status_panel_1", "status_panel_2"). Every id must be unique, groups included.
workspace_fields.layout_weights: Each panel or group id from layout_shape and its size: a proportional share of the group it sits in, so a weight-2 pane gets twice the room of a weight-1 neighbour. An id left out gets 1; the top group fills the page and needs none.
workspace_fields.background: Optional. The moving background behind the panels, e.g. {"visual": "network_mesh", "blur": 6}. false turns it off; leave it out for the usual still network.

settings_fields.model_sprites: Which parts of the model canvases are drawn (1 = drawn). Submarine map: boat_in through ocean. HVAC house: background through indicator. Turn these on in any workspace that shows those models.
settings_fields.model_colors: Colors for the model canvases, as theme color names ("field", "red", ...) or hex codes. Submarine map: ocean through boat_out_outline. HVAC house: background through hotness.
settings_fields.strip_chart_sprites: Not used by the game yet.
settings_fields.strip_chart_colors: Colors for the strip charts: background and grid, one color per plotted line in "paths", and the live-value markers in "heads".
settings_fields.strip_chart_auto_fit: 1 starts every strip chart (ModBus Monitors, Defender Monitors, the network graph's rate chart) in fit mode, zoomed to fit the recent data. Students can toggle it.
settings_fields.strip_chart_auto_fit_max_seconds: How many seconds of history fit mode shows at most.
settings_fields.game_progress: Records which network forms the student has started. Not read by the game yet.
settings_fields.network_action_form_inputs: What starts out typed into each network action form's text boxes, in order (e.g. "arp": [target IP, host IP]).
settings_fields.network_action_forms_shown: Which network action forms start out shown (1). Students can change this with Show Forms. A form only appears if "available" also offers it.
settings_fields.available: What this workspace offers at all (1 = offered). Network action forms: wifi, nmap, arp, dos, sniff, nfq, ap_connect, encryption, ap_tunnel, kalman. ModBus table forms: table, modify. Defender ModBus forms: mode, sliders. Models in the model panel: hvac, submarine, defender_hvac, defender_submarine - and auto_switch offers the checkbox that follows the AP's reported mode. A form also needs its *_forms_shown entry to start out showing.
settings_fields.modbus_table_forms_shown: Which ModBus table panel forms start out shown: "table" (live register values) and "modify" (rewriting values in transit).
settings_fields.defender_modbus_forms_shown: Which defender ModBus panel forms start out shown: "mode" and "sliders".
settings_fields.modbus_model_selected: Which model the model panel starts on. If it isn't available here, the panel starts on the first one that is.
settings_fields.modbus_model_auto_switch: 1 starts with the defender models following the AP's reported mode automatically.
settings_fields.modbus_packet_modify_enabled: 1 lets the packet interceptor rewrite ModBus values in transit, using each register's multiplier and offset. Students turn this on and off from the modify form.
settings_fields.modbus_registers: Settings for each ModBus register (hreg_1 to hreg_15): "show" puts it in the table and charts; "nickname" and "units" name it; "factor" scales raw values for display; "modify" lets the interceptor rewrite it, using "multiplier" and "offset". "label" is its labels key.
settings_fields.packet_console: "mode": "live" shows packets as they arrive, "paused" freezes the packet console and network graph. "summary" is the plain-language description of the current packet filter.
settings_fields.packet_filter_categories: How the packet filter's checkboxes are grouped, and which checkboxes each group has.
settings_fields.packet_filter_checkboxes: Which packet filters start out ticked (1). Nothing ticked shows every packet.
settings_fields.packet_filter_entries: What starts out typed into the packet filter's text boxes, like an address to filter by.
settings_fields.packet_columns: Which packet console columns are shown (1). Students can change this with Show Columns.

settings_keys._note: One explanation per key inside each settings field, shown as a tooltip on that key's name in the Workspace Config Editor. Nested like _default.json; a "*" entry covers every key at that level that has no entry of its own (e.g. every hreg_N). A nested object's own "_note" explains its heading.

model_sprites.boat_in: Submarine map: the vessel where the device reports it is (the incoming, possibly spoofed, value).
model_sprites.boat_out: Submarine map: the vessel where the controller is commanding it to be (the outgoing value).
model_sprites.path_in: Submarine map: the trail behind the reported (incoming) vessel.
model_sprites.path_out: Submarine map: the trail behind the commanded (outgoing) vessel.
model_sprites.boat_in_label: Submarine map: the text label beside the reported vessel.
model_sprites.boat_out_label: Submarine map: the text label beside the commanded vessel.
model_sprites.boat_in_position: Submarine map: the coordinate readout for the reported vessel.
model_sprites.boat_out_position: Submarine map: the coordinate readout for the commanded vessel.
model_sprites.grid_numbers: Submarine map: the numbers along the grid lines.
model_sprites.room_thermostat: HVAC house: the thermostat on the room wall, showing the room temperature.
model_sprites.vent: HVAC house: the vent, which shows heating or cooling airflow.
model_sprites.controller_thermostat: HVAC house: the controller's own temperature readout.
model_sprites.indicator: HVAC house: the heating/cooling indicator light.

model_colors.grid_axes: Submarine map: color of the two center axes.
model_colors.path_in: Submarine map: trail color behind the reported (incoming) vessel.
model_colors.boat_in_fill: Submarine map: fill color of the reported vessel.
model_colors.boat_in_outline: Submarine map: outline color of the reported vessel.
model_colors.path_out: Submarine map: trail color behind the commanded (outgoing) vessel.
model_colors.boat_out_fill: Submarine map: fill color of the commanded vessel.
model_colors.boat_out_outline: Submarine map: outline color of the commanded vessel.
model_colors.line_art: HVAC house: outline color for the drawing.
model_colors.fill: HVAC house: fill color for walls and boxes.
model_colors.coldness: HVAC house: color used for cooling and cold temperatures.
model_colors.hotness: HVAC house: color used for heating and hot temperatures.

strip_chart_sprites.*: Not used by the game yet.

strip_chart_colors.paths: One color per plotted line, used in order. One color per line in this box.
strip_chart_colors.heads: Colors of the live-value markers at the end of each line, used in order.

game_progress.*: Set to 1 once the student starts this network action form. Recorded but not read by the game yet.

network_action_form_inputs.wifi: Wi-Fi form: the "Device Name" box - the network to connect to.
network_action_form_inputs.arp: ARP spoofing form: the target IP, then the host IP to impersonate. One per line.
network_action_form_inputs.sniff: Not used - the sniffing form has no text boxes.
network_action_form_inputs.dos: Denial of service form: its two "Target IP:Port" boxes, in order. One per line.
network_action_form_inputs.ap_connect: AP connect form: the access point's address, e.g. http://192.168.4.1.
network_action_form_inputs.encryption: Encryption form: the starting encryption key.

network_action_forms_shown.wifi: Wi-Fi form: connects this computer to a wireless network.
network_action_forms_shown.nmap: Nmap form: scans the network for devices.
network_action_forms_shown.arp: ARP spoofing form: poisons ARP tables to put this computer in the middle of traffic.
network_action_forms_shown.dos: Denial of service form: floods a target with traffic.
network_action_forms_shown.sniff: Sniffing form: captures packets into the packet console.
network_action_forms_shown.nfq: Packet interceptor form (NetFilterQueue): holds packets so they can be read or rewritten in transit.
network_action_forms_shown.ap_connect: AP connect form: connects to the access point and shows whether it's connected. Every other defender form talks through this connection.
network_action_forms_shown.encryption: Encryption form: turns AP-level encryption on or off with a key.
network_action_forms_shown.ap_tunnel: AP tunnel form: routes device traffic only through the AP, so there's no directly attackable TCP/ModBus.
network_action_forms_shown.kalman: Kalman filter form: turns the AP's Kalman filter on or off for its current mode. Usually left hidden - the Defender Flags panel has the same toggle.

modbus_table_forms_shown.modify: The form for rewriting register values in transit.

*._note: Settings for this one holding register.
*.label: The labels key for this register's name.
*.show: 1 shows this register in the ModBus table and charts.
*.nickname: A short name shown instead of the register number, like "heading".
*.factor: Raw values are multiplied by this for display, e.g. 0.1 to show 235 as 23.5.
*.units: Units shown after the value, like "deg" or "C".
*.multiplier: When modify is on, the interceptor multiplies this register's value by this in transit.
*.offset: When modify is on, the interceptor adds this to the value in transit, after the multiplier.
*.modify: 1 lets the packet interceptor rewrite this register (needs modbus_packet_modify_enabled).

packet_console.mode: "live" shows packets as they arrive; "paused" freezes the packet console and network graph.
packet_console.summary: The plain-language description of the current packet filter, shown to the student.
packet_console.function: The packet filter as Python code, rebuilt by the filter overlay. Leave this alone.
packet_console.secret explanation for awful coding prac: A developer note, not a setting.

packet_filter_categories.hack: Checkboxes in the "which tool caught it" group. One per line.
packet_filter_categories.layers: Checkboxes in the protocol layer group. One per line.
packet_filter_categories.direction: Checkboxes in the direction group. One per line.

packet_filter_checkboxes.nmap: Show packets from the Nmap scan.
packet_filter_checkboxes.arp: Show packets caught by ARP spoofing.
packet_filter_checkboxes.dos: Show packets from the denial of service attack.
packet_filter_checkboxes.nfq: Show packets caught by the packet interceptor.
packet_filter_checkboxes.pcap: Show packets loaded from a capture file.
packet_filter_checkboxes.misc: Not in any group in packet_filter_categories, so it has no checkbox and does nothing.
packet_filter_checkboxes.MODBUSPDU03READHOLDINGREGISTERSREQUEST: Show ModBus read holding registers requests.
packet_filter_checkboxes.MODBUSPDU03READHOLDINGREGISTERSRESPONSE: Show ModBus read holding registers responses.
packet_filter_checkboxes.MODBUSPDU06WRITESINGLEREGISTERREQUEST: Show ModBus write single register requests.
packet_filter_checkboxes.MODBUSPDU06WRITESINGLEREGISTERRESPONSE: Show ModBus write single register responses.
packet_filter_checkboxes.other: Not in any group in packet_filter_categories, so it has no checkbox and does nothing.

packet_filter_entries.address_filter: Only show packets to or from this address. Empty shows every address.

packet_columns.time_word: Time the packet arrived, to 4 decimal places.
packet_columns.number: The packet's number in the capture.
packet_columns.observer: What saw the packet: the tool's name, or which side of the interceptor (prerouting/postrouting nfq).
packet_columns.hack: Which tool caught it: arp, sniff, dos, nfq or nmap.
packet_columns.summary: Scapy's one-line summary of the packet.
packet_columns.mac_word: Source and destination MAC as "source -> destination".
packet_columns.ip_word: Source and destination IP as "source -> destination".
packet_columns.variables: ModBus: the registers the packet touches.
packet_columns.values: ModBus: the register values it carries.
packet_columns.command: ModBus: the full command name, like "read holding registers response".
packet_columns.is_modbus: Whether the packet has a ModBus layer.
packet_columns.is_useful: Whether the packet changes a register value.
packet_columns.is_primary: Whether it's the first request or response of its ModBus transaction.
packet_columns.command_word: ModBus: the short command, like "Write Request".

available.dos: Network action form: denial of service.
available.kalman: Network action form: Kalman filter toggle.
available.table: ModBus table panel form: the live register table.
available.modify: ModBus table panel form: rewriting values in transit.
available.mode: Defender ModBus panel form: the AP's current mode.
available.sliders: Defender ModBus panel form: filter-tuning sliders.
available.hvac: Model panel: the HVAC house, driven by intercepted ModBus traffic.
available.submarine: Model panel: the submarine map, driven by intercepted ModBus traffic.
available.auto_switch: Model panel: the checkbox that switches models to follow the AP's reported mode.
available.defender_hvac: Model panel: the defender's HVAC house, driven by the AP's reports.
available.defender_submarine: Model panel: the defender's submarine map, driven by the AP's reports.

defender_modbus_forms_shown.mode: The read-only display of the AP's current mode (submarine or HVAC).
defender_modbus_forms_shown.sliders: The filter-tuning sliders for the AP's current mode.
